features.name: Net Square
features.now: Presence works: the server, the transports on every system, and a prototype Square where other players walk as NPCs.
features.left: Move the way in to a gate in Lan's HP, rebuild the Square from BN6's own pieces, and make the people in it talkable.

features.name: Trade
features.now: Designed: counters at Trade Central in the Square, the server commits a trade, and the swap is applied after the visit returns, with BN6's own give and take chips.
features.left: All of it: the counters, the server's commit, the swap in the live game, and a pending file that holds CONTINUE until the trade settles.

features.name: Arena
features.now: NetBattles from the Net Square between two games, each running both linked cores, only keys crossing the server, the pair hashed every 60 frames. Full rules for two games with BN5's ROM: BN5's installs written down as the game's core makes them and made again in both pair cores, BN5's chips and Souls carried; UNITE's Soul carried to the other GBA by the pair. Proven on two clients: MrkCan1 and KnightSoul on both screens with every hash agreeing.
features.left: The other five Souls, Chaos Unison, ColonelSoul's button and BN5's mood in a NetBattle seen on both GBAs; a marker that wanders against a moving target checked against BN5; rollback.

features.name: Two MegaMen a side
features.now: A side-by-side team match from the Net Square (protocol v15: four seats over the server, ARENA_SEAT, the stands' four streams) and the dev flag's (--dev arena2v2): four MegaMen on BN6's field in the Arena's pair, the partners' keys two more streams of the Arena's input (players 2 and 3), sampled on their side's GBA's frames as its pad is and carried in that GBA's own link packets (the two bytes +5 and +7 BN6 never writes or reads, written at the pad's store 0x0801FF8C and read out of both sides' received packets 0x020399F0), so that both GBAs take a partner's word from the exchange that brings his lead's pad, at the same iteration; guessed and rolled back as the other player's. Each partner has his own battle NaviStats and hand, answered by object; picks his chips on BN6's own Custom screen on a plain copy of the pair his own client keeps, from his own deck, which each GBA deals and keeps from the packets' words alone; the leads wait for him by BN6's own link wait, the limit said in his place by his side's GBA. His whole MegaMan: his NaviCust compiled by BN6's own reload (on every game of a match from the MegaMan he sent), his Crosses and Beast Out on his own screen and run by BN6's crossing for his object, a Program Advance joined in his hand as BN6 joins it; UNITE with his own Souls on his own screen (BN5's installs' hooks on his copy's GBA), his Soul crossing in his stream into his own Souls block, its life, powers and look by object. Under full rules BN5's chip AI's rooms, the Chaos Unison, a Soul's powers and look, BN5's mood and DarkChip rule answer by object. Proved on both GBAs, through rollbacks and mutations, and over a local server with four games and a spectator (a partner never picking, a Cross, a PA, Beast Out with 40 ms lag and 30 ms jitter, a slow partner, a drop).
features.left: ColonelSoul's button for a partner pressed (built; his ColonelSoul's unison proved), the Dark Soul's lists from his own folder, the green flash's tint and a hit's mood gain by object; a real network, the deployed server, devices; a partner's NaviCust compiled on games of different runs; WhiCapsl's and Uninstll's marks and a chip of computed power in his hand.

features.name: BN6's sound engine
features.now: MP2K (m4a) as BN6's code runs it, in the engine's own C, plays the title's and the PET screens' songs and sounds: the same as the game byte for byte, frame by frame, for every song and sound checked against the plain ROM in romlab (tools/mp2k_verify.py). BN5's songs play on the same code, BN5's library being BN6's; the Jukebox plays both games' music players.
features.left: Where BN5's own songs 0x06-0x09, 0x11, 0x12, 0x18 and 0x20-0x24 play (its cutscene scripts unread), for their names; a frame-by-frame differential of a BN5 song against BN5's own engine state (its RAM's places).

since.what: The engine's MP2K reads each player's song from its own ROM (mp2k_read, a player's and a channel's ROM; the library's tables BN6's, mp2k_lib_u8): the Jukebox's songs of BN6 and BN5 (docs/PET.md). A song just begun counts as busy (MPlayStart's status 0 before its first tick), or a PET screen's sound over the held game never started.

The PET menu's labels: their tiles 0x086C8058 (90, uncompressed), the PET's load list's entry for them 0x08120A9C (source, 0x0600D340, 0xB40), the table of each entry's label 0x08121394 (9 x 2 tile entries each, ChipFolder to Save, then Status), each label's letters in colour 5 + its entry shaded in 3 (9 of 882 shaded pixels off the rule, hand-drawn), Comm's grey store 0x08120F2A, VRAM 0x0600DE80-0x0600DFFF zero in the PET and on the map; Comm relabelled Options from the labels' own letters (pet_options.c, letters.c) and its A taken for the game's Options

experiments.name: BN5's MP2K library against BN6's
experiments.result: From SoundMain (BN5 0x0814C9FC, BN6 0x0814F754) the next 0x2104 bytes differ in 24 literal words (the seven tables', the jump template's, the player and song tables', one RAM address) and 35 pointers moved by the block's move, 0x2D58; the tables (BN5 0x081BC74C-0x081BC930) equal BN6's; the m4aSoundMode word is 0x0093040D in both (BN5 0x08000568). BN5's title through the engine against the plain BN5 ROM in romlab, 20 s: envelopes at 0.90, octave bands within 0.7 dB to 12 kHz; BN6's title against it, 0.42 and 2.9 dB. BN6's 0x01, 0x13 and 0x66 still byte for byte the game's after the engine read songs per ROM.
experiments.meaning: BN5's songs play as BN5 plays them on BN6's code and tables, their data from BN5's ROM.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: a partner's own Custom screen, BN6's own
experiments.result: A lone core loaded from his side's GBA at a Custom screen shows Lan's 'Communication error' within frames; a plain copy of the pair (both GBAs on their own cable, no hook) copied in each turn, his deck written into BN6_BATTLE_DECK and BN6_BATTLE_STEP put back to 0, has BN6 set its Custom screen up anew with his chips (BusterUp, Sword, Cannon, Atk+10, MiniBomb where his lead's offers a Cannon A first) and take his keys by its own rules; OK takes BN6_CUSTOM_MODE to 0x08 with his picks read (3 and 4). His picks crossed as pick messages in his stream and went into his hand on both GBAs at the same iteration: 1,315 iterations 0 apart with 135 rollbacks and with none, all 26 hashes the same; arenaroll=8 200 of 200 the same, its 26 hashes the delay alone's; his hand a chip short on the second GBA alone parts them from iteration 201. A frame of his screen 1.37 to 1.41 ms, a turn's copy 0.12 to 0.15 ms, making it once 160 ms. The normal NetBattle unchanged (frame 2690, 86d2f837337a1494).
experiments.meaning: A partner needs no GBA of his own in the pair: BN6's own Custom screen runs on his client alone, and the battle stays deterministic because only his picks cross.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: the leads wait for their partners
experiments.result: BN6's link battle closes its Custom screen once both GBAs' packets (bn6f sub_800B3A2, 0x0800B3A2: the mark 0x56789123, the hand, the NaviStats, the Cross's record) have come over the cable, checked each frame of mode 0x14 at 0x08026DEC; holding a side's packet back until its partner's picks are in makes both GBAs wait by BN6's own cable (the other shows BN6's Cstmzing... over the held side). A partner 10 s slow each turn: 3,035 iterations 0 apart, 91 hashes the same with 482 rollbacks and with none, arenaroll=8 683 of 683; a partner who never picks is ended by his client's send at 3,480 frames held, a client gone quiet by the pair's own limit at 3,600 (216 hashes the same with and without rollbacks). The normal NetBattle unchanged (frame 2690, 86d2f837337a1494).
experiments.meaning: A partner can be waited for without any clock: the hold is read in the side's GBA's RAM and crosses by BN6's own link, so every client and spectator agrees on the moment the screen closes.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: a partner's NaviCust compiled by BN6
experiments.result: BN6's reload of MegaMan's stats from the NaviCust's board (bn6f reloadCurNaviStatBoosts_813c3ac, Gregar 0x0813E18C) called once through the game's update on a plain core loaded from the checkpoint, the partner's loadout written in: a board of Custom1, UnderShirt and HP+100 (base 360) gives HP 460, Custom 6, UnderShirt 1, as the run's own menus made them. His record takes it whole (but for the start form and the BeastOutCounter a link battle's start sets; each GBA's own menu NaviStats and its side's battle record measured the same, all 0x64 bytes): side 1's partner set up with 460 HP beside his lead's 100, his own screen dealing six chips where his lead's deals five. 2,686 iterations 0 apart, 56 hashes the same with 289 rollbacks and with none; arenaroll=8 440 of 440 the same, its 58 hashes the delay alone's; the records their sides' copies on the second GBA alone part them from iteration 1.
experiments.meaning: A partner's NaviCust needs no rules of ours: BN6's own compile runs for him on his client, and only its result crosses.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: a partner's own Cross
experiments.result: BN6's crossing controller (0x020367F0) crosses its two records' objects alone; with its turn check sent to the crossing where a partner has a Cross (0x080148C0), his object asked to cross at its step's first frame and waited for (0x08014944: 0x4000 into his AI data's +0x44, the wait on +0x48's 0x80) and the pending form answered his own where the crossing object is his (0x0801595E), both partners cross into HeatCross at the first turn while their leads stay, on both GBAs. 3,854 iterations 0 apart, 88 hashes the same with 430 rollbacks and with none; arenaroll=8 666 of 666 the same, its 88 hashes the delay alone's; his Cross none on the second GBA alone parts them from iteration 1. The step's wait first returned with HOOK_RETURN into a caller that reached it by mov lr,pc; bx r1 (lr's Thumb bit clear): the game ran ARM and stopped on the black crossing screen; a jump to lr | 1 mends it. His pending form is taken as the controller's mode 8 begins, as BN6 takes its records'; kept to his next turn, the check as a turn's change begins met it again and crossed him anew.
experiments.meaning: BN6's own crossing runs for a third and fourth MegaMan from three hooks; his choice is a message of his stream.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: a partner's Program Advance
experiments.result: Cannon A, B and C picked in order on his own screen: BN6's OK (0x08029110) makes Z-Canon1 (0x140) through its check (0x08029520), its next mode 0x10, the hand it builds at 0x020366C0 chips 0x140, 0xFFFF, 0x0001, powers 300, 0, 40. His client finds the place and count the pair's own build gives that hand from (picks 0 to 2) and crosses them before his picks; both GBAs write his hand Z-Canon1, power 300; his Z-Canon1 takes side 1's partner from 421 to 121 and side 1's player from 78 to 0. 1,284 iterations 0 apart, 33 hashes the same with 163 rollbacks and with none; arenaroll=8 254 of 254 the same; the PA left out on the second GBA alone parts them at iteration 4.
experiments.meaning: BN6's OK decides his Program Advance on his screen; what crosses is where it joined his picks.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: a partner's Beast Out, its turns as a lead's
experiments.result: Gregar's emblem commits a Beast Out into the same record as CROSSSELECT (0x08029344: form 0xB), so a partner's crosses as his Cross does. BN6 counts a form's turns for each side's player alone (0x08015A16 as each screen opens, 0x08015A38 as the crossing controller is done) and asks a Beast Out's end for the controller's records alone (0x080159C6, 0x08015994, mode 8's wait 0x08014A00): the two counts' ends hooked and their bodies entered again with his object, the end asked from the turn check's end by calling BN6's routines back to the hook. Control: the leads taking Beast Out by the same keys, each lead and his partner in form 0xB with the same BeastOutCounter at every turn's check (3, 2 at iteration 1084, 1 at 1897). 2,173 iterations 0 apart, 52 hashes the same with 261 rollbacks and with none; arenaroll=8 396 of 396 the same; none on the second GBA parts them from iteration 1; the leads too: 2,902 iterations 0 apart, 104 hashes the same with 524 rollbacks and without. With all four in Beast Out under the delay alone (arenawindow=0, and arenaroll=8 over it) the GBAs part at iteration 2305 of 2,375, the partners' keys 46 iterations late: the same with the partners' turn hooks off, so the GBAs drift past the rings' delay.
experiments.meaning: A partner's Beast Out is BN6's own, his turns counted by BN6's routines run for him; the rings' delay meets its first limit in a lead's Beast Out under the stall.

experiments.name: What BN6 has to show a mood, for the Square's emotes
experiments.result: BN6 has no emotion-bubble set: frame 0 of every sprite of lists 4-9 and the first frame of 452 icon-sized animations of lists 0-5, 7 and 9 drawn from Gregar show no ?, note, sweat, anger or sleep mark; its one heart is Roll's (list 3's 0x50), its one burst the battle's counter-hit "!!" (list 5's 0x07: "!!", a bat, a skull). MegaMan's overworld sprite (list 6's 0x37) has 73 animations: the item-get pose 0x18 (Gregar's text F8 01 18 41 times, 20 followed by sound 0x73), the arrival 0x2D (cutscene 47 00 FF 2D then sound 0x76), arms raised 0x40, sparks 0x38, panting 0x42, a leap 0x43, the buster aimed 0x33-0x36. BN6's hop in place (NPC bytes 22 11 60 DC 21) is in Gregar 157 times. A chat box face has three animations (still, blinking, talking; Lan's a fourth, eyes shut), set by text F5 03 n (31 times in Gregar's plain text), and no second face for a mood. BN5 adds a heart (list 4's 0x26) and a music note (list 4's 0x44).
experiments.meaning: An emote can be a pose of the peer's own MegaMan puppet (an animation number, no NPC slot) or a hop, in step for everyone from the emote's index; a mark over a head needs one of the Square's 16 NPC slots, all taken, or (not yet tried) a map object, 56 slots, drawn through an OverworldMapObjects id left unused.

experiments.name: Issue #182: DarkInvs on side 1 of a 1v1 NetBattle
experiments.result: Real: on both GBAs side 1's DarkInvs moved his AI data into the one block of BN5's size side 0's player holds ("side 0 020115e0 side 1 020115e0"), side 0 turned grey and the battle stood still. An actor's AI data is not its object slot's: BN6 keeps a pool of eight (0x02034080, its bits at 0x0203F6A0, taken by 0x0800ED2C, let go by 0x0800ED80 through the entry's own bit at +0x7C). With a room of its own for each MegaMan at the pool's end (side 1's player 0x02034740), side 1 fights under the chip AI and side 0 as himself (over at frame 1179), both sides at once too; 147 rollbacks of 8 the same; two a side with all four under it 2,372 iterations 0 apart, 319 rollbacks the same, chipaibreak=2 apart from iteration 340; the ordinary NetBattle over at 2690, last hash 86d2f837337a1494.
experiments.meaning: BN5's chip AI is safe for any MegaMan of a NetBattle; a room is refused (he is left out) only where actors hold the pool's last entries.

experiments.name: The full-rules audit by object
experiments.result: A partner charging B in his lead's Chaos Unison now fires his own charged shot (both GBAs: "side 0's partner's charged B his own"), 3,123 iterations 0 apart, 456 rollbacks the same, partnerbreak=2 (the old rule on one GBA) apart from iteration 222; a partner's BN5 DarkChip darkens him in his own Souls' block (0x0203FFBE, 0x0203FFDE) and NaviStats (the effect slots 30 and 31), not his lead. The five BN5 chips the audit named never ask BN6's side-player getter (their copy of BN5's 0x080125EE, a side's player's chaos flag, is never called); BN5's Navis that ask stand in no NetBattle.
experiments.meaning: The Souls' and the mood's hooks are by object; a partner's UNITE has its block waiting. Nothing in a NetBattle aims at a side's player alone through the getter.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side (epic #167's spike)
experiments.result: With a side's second MegaMan's keys written at the battle loop's key copy (0x08012DFC) by the loop's iteration, both GBAs' battles agree at every iteration: the research harness over a whole battle (every T1, T3 and T4 object, AI data, NaviStats, hand and random number compared; nothing apart beyond BN6's own 1v1's fields) and the pair under --dev rollbench,arena2v2 (489 iterations, 0 apart, 11 rollbacks the same); one key flipped on one GBA parts them (325 apart). The feasibility study's one-frame skew was its harness: every mode it ran was mode 1, which scheduled the partner by each core's own frame counter, a frame or two apart at the same iteration.
experiments.meaning: BN6's engine runs two MegaMen a side alike on both GBAs; a partner's keys must enter by the battle's iteration. Under full rules BN5's chip AI gave both of side 0's MegaMen one AI data block, which the flag keeps to the first.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: the partners as streams
experiments.result: --dev arena,arenaboth,arena2v2=1 at delay 1: with 107 rollbacks (lag 4, window 8) and with none (lag 0) the battle ends at frame 2690 with all 44 hashes the same; the GBAs agree at all 2,399 iterations, 0 of the partners' takes late; arenaroll=8 rolls back 335 times, the game's state the same each time, its 44 hashes the delay alone's; a key flipped on the second GBA at iteration 300 parts the GBAs at 2,100 iterations. A NetBattle without the flag ends as before (frame 2690, 86d2f837337a1494).
experiments.meaning: A partner's keys can cross a network as a stream of their own and enter BN6 at the battle's iteration on both GBAs; rollback covers them since the rings are core RAM.

experiments.name: Two MegaMen a side: the partners' own NaviStats and hands
experiments.result: With BN6's battle NaviStats routine (0x08013682) and hand routine (0x08010018) answered by object for asks that pass the object in r5, each partner reads and writes his own record and hand, kept in two effect slots taken in BN6's pool (0x02036710): given 150 max HP both partners are set up with 150 while their leads keep 100, hits take each from his own; each partner uses the Cannon of his own hand (his chip up next 0 to 1, his lead's staying at 0, the icon leaving him alone), side 1's taking side 0's from 84 to 43; both GBAs agree at all 2,399 iterations, with 221 rollbacks and without them all 44 hashes the same, arenaroll=8 335 of 335 the same; the records on one GBA alone part them from iteration 1.
experiments.meaning: BN6's one NaviStats and one hand a side are answered by object without touching its code, the room taken from BN6's own object pool, since the RAM the project has free holds one record.

experiments.name: A rematch in a second: BN6's random numbers at a link battle's start
experiments.result: Both random words (0x020013F0, 0x02001120) read on both GBAs of the pair a frame at a time through the way in's last two steps: alike on the two GBAs all the way, stepped as on a map until Practice's last confirm; 19 frames after that press the battle draws the first word once and keeps it, 71 frames on puts it back as its opening ends, and the folders are shuffled from the second the frame after. Both words written from a seed at the start of that step change both GBAs' first hands (seed 7: 1636 2448 2448 0201 0605; seed 8: 0236 3459 34af 009a 0236; none: 0001 34c0 0236 0201 2447) and every one of the battle's 44 hashes; the pair kept at that step and gone into again with seed 8 deals seed 8's hands and gives its 44 hashes byte for byte, 244 frames of the pair instead of 1,817.
experiments.meaning: A rematch needs no new way in: the pair kept where the bout's seed goes in, and the seed (the battle's ID, known to both players and every spectator) makes each bout its own.

experiments.name: Inputs only, two cores per client
experiments.result: Completes at 0, 50, 100 and 150 ms one-way delay, every battle timer as the original; a flipped input and a killed peer both stop the fight.
experiments.meaning: The Arena's design: each client runs both games, only inputs travel.

experiments.name: Snapshot of the pair
experiments.result: Restored at six points and replayed 1, 4 and 8 frames, twice each: every replay exact; 863,016 bytes, 1.2 ms a restore on the desktop.
experiments.meaning: Rollback is possible, but only with more than mGBA's own state save.

experiments.name: A carried chip in the pair
experiments.result: Cannon A, given by BN6's own routine, chosen and hitting for 40 in Practice.
experiments.meaning: A run's chip fights natively; the installer for a whole loadout is still to build.

experiments.name: BN5 in both pair cores, two clients
experiments.result: The same installs' record on both (1,913,709 bytes, 132 hooks) and the same ready hash; Alpha's MrkCan1 took Beta from 100 to 30 on both screens, every hash agreeing to the end; a desync and two records apart each stopped both.
experiments.meaning: Two games with BN5's ROM make byte-identical pairs from their own ROMs; a difference in the installs is caught at the ready.

experiments.name: UNITE across the cable
experiments.result: Both GBAs number the sides alike (BN6_BATTLE_SIDE 0 on the challenger's core, 1 on the other's); with the committed Soul carried at the frame's end both cores read side 0 in form 8 with Soul 11 from the same frame, and both screens drew KnightMan's summon and KnightSoul, 36 hashes agreeing.
experiments.meaning: BN6's link carries the form and not the Soul; the pair carries the Soul, and the look is drawn by the side the sprite selector's caller draws.

experiments.name: Two games through the hosted server
experiments.result: The same room built from seed 120 on both; 211 peer positions matched; round trips 33 to 49 ms; both MegaMen back unchanged, all 24 checkpoint files unchanged.
experiments.meaning: Presence over the public internet works, and a visit leaves the save alone.

experiments.name: Sixteen games, two full channels
experiments.result: 10,248 peer positions matched; every game's loadout back after a disconnect; 192 checkpoint files unchanged.
experiments.meaning: A full room holds on one machine; not a measure of handhelds or a busy network.

experiments.name: Browser and native game together
experiments.result: Both built the same room; 578 browser and 592 native peer positions matched.
experiments.meaning: The browser build can share a Square with the native ones.

experiments.name: Retroid Pocket Nova on the public server
experiments.result: Same room as a desktop peer; 189 handheld positions matched; round trips 40 to 47 ms; a 1,000 HP checkpoint back unchanged.
experiments.meaning: The PortMaster build visits as the desktop does; the only physical handheld tried.

experiments.name: ROM-free cable on every desktop and the Nova
experiments.result: 256 transfers and all 1,024 received words right on Linux, Windows x64, macOS ARM64 and the Nova.
experiments.meaning: mGBA's lockstep cable links two cores on every system tried.

experiments.name: Practice on one pair of cores
experiments.result: BN6's Practice unpatched: 18,855 serial transfers, 100 to 0, both back at the menu, all 1,433 battle frames agreeing.
experiments.meaning: BN6's own NetBattle runs on two linked cores without help.

experiments.name: Serial words sent over a socket
experiments.result: Completes at no delay; at 50, 100 and 150 ms only 95, 48 and 35 battle frames in a minute.
experiments.meaning: The cable cannot be split across the network.

experiments.name: Spare chips read from the Pack
experiments.result: Six folder scenarios through BN6's own folder editor agreed with the reader; six planted faults caught.
experiments.meaning: Which copies are spare (the Pack less every folder's copies) can be read exactly; the rule is kept at commit 7b4b8ef.

rules: The player's ROM is only read; saves, states and traces stay under .build/.
Network work runs against the project's own server and the developer's own games, never anyone else's service or account.
No masks: a difference between the original and ours is explained or it fails.
No Tango code is read or used.

glossary.meaning: The online place players visit between acts; other players walk in it as NPCs.
BN6's own homepage map, where MegaMan arrives after every act; the Square's gate is to stand there.
The Square's counters where two players are to swap chips.
NetBattles between players, BN6's own fights over the network.
Two mGBA cores joined by an emulated link cable, both games running on one client.
BN6's NetBattle choice that costs no chip; the fight every experiment scripts.
Each frame waits until both players' inputs for it have arrived.
Run ahead on a guessed input, then rewind to a snapshot and replay when the real one arrives.
Everything needed to resume the pair exactly: both cores, both flash saves, the cable.
The unchanged original, run the same way, that ours is compared against.
A deliberate break, to show the comparison catches it.
The game's own state after boot, before a run changes anything; made on each machine, never committed.
